chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from al-Muthanna al-Hannat, from Qutayba al-A'sha, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from a freed slave of the Banu Shayban clan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
When our Qa'im rises, God will place His hand upon the heads of the servants, so He gathers their intellects through it, and their understanding becomes complete through him.

key_terms.أَحْلَام: Understanding, forbearance, mature discernment (plural of hilm) — often paired with 'aql in ethical discourse
key_terms.عُقُول: Intellects, rational faculties (plural of 'aql) — the capacity for reason and religious understanding
key_terms.قَائِمُنَا: Our Qa'im — the title for the awaited twelfth Imam (Imam al-Mahdi) who will rise to establish justice

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about the intellect of people when the Qa'im (Imam Mahdi) rises?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) describes the transformative spiritual effect of the Qa'im's — the awaited Imam Mahdi's — rising. When the Qa'im appears, God will directly elevate the intellectual and spiritual capacity of all people by placing His hand upon their heads, a metaphorical act signifying divine bestowal of wisdom and cognitive perfection. The phrase 'their understanding (ahlam) becomes complete' indicates that human rationality and moral discernment will reach their fullest potential in that era of universal justice.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Al Musna Al Hannat, from Quteyba Al A’asha, from Ibn Abu Yafour, from a slave of the Clan of Shayban, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said;

‘When our<sup>asws</sup> Qaim<sup>asws</sup> rises, and he<sup>asws</sup> places his<sup>asws</sup> hand upon the heads of the servants, so their intellects would be gathered by it and complete their understanding (of the religion)’.
